In-scope systems.value: RMA data-call calendar maintained in the internal regulatory system; deadline sources are the RMA PASS/eDAS cutoff schedule, Appendix III and rma.usda.gov bulletin postings

Compliance procedure documented.value: FCIC Data Call & Deadline Tracking Procedure — bulletin monitoring, 3-business-day calendar entry of new data calls, owner assignment, reminder configuration and cutoff-date change control

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; re-approved before each July 1 reinsurance-year start and on any SRA amendment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Weekly transaction cutoff dates from the M13 schedule, Plan of Operations by April 1 preceding the reinsurance year, monthly Appendix III accounting reports, and per-data-call due dates including 'within 45 days' correction windows

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts at T-10/T-5/T-1 business days before every weekly cutoff and monthly report, and T-60/T-30/T-10 before the April 1 Plan of Operations

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every missed-deadline remediation and every calendar-control change

checklist.step: Build the reinsurance-year obligation inventory from the SRA itself
actions: Open the executed 2026 SRA and read Sections III and IV plus Appendix II (Plan of Operations) and Appendix III (M13 Data Acceptance System Handbook), listing every reporting obligation on its own inventory row.

For each row record: obligation name, SRA/appendix citation, frequency (weekly, monthly, annual, event-driven), the due-date rule (e.g. 'by April 1 preceding the reinsurance year', 'no later than the weekly transaction cutoff') and the receiving RMA system (PASS/eDAS, Plan of Operations application, escrow reporting).
Ask the Reinsurance Manager for any company-specific conditions in the SRA signature documents or fund designations that add reporting items, and add them.
Load the inventory into the internal regulatory system tagged REG-056 with the reinsurance year (July 1 - June 30).
checklist.done: every SRA reporting obligation has an inventory row with citation, frequency, due-date rule and receiving RMA system.

checklist.step: Subscribe the team to RMA's bulletin and memoranda distributions
actions: On rma.usda.gov open Laws & Regulations ▸ Bulletins and Memoranda and subscribe the team mailbox to Manager's Bulletins (MGR), Product Management Bulletins (PM) and Informational Memoranda via the GovDelivery email signup.
Confirm the subscription lands in the shared Regulatory Reporting mailbox, not an individual's inbox, so coverage survives absence.
Record the subscription date and the covered series in the procedure document.
Name a primary and backup reader for the mailbox in the team rota.
checklist.done: the shared mailbox receives MGR/PM bulletins and memoranda, with a named primary and backup reader.

checklist.step: Sweep RMA bulletins weekly and log each one against the calendar
actions: Every Monday open rma.usda.gov ▸ Bulletins and Memoranda, filter to the current year, and compare against the bulletin log's last-reviewed entry.
For each new bulletin record number, title, issue date and a one-line relevance call (new data call / deadline change / no reporting impact).
Save each relevant bulletin as PDF named <bulletin-no>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the REG-056 evidence folder.
Where a bulletin creates or moves a deadline, open a calendar change request the same day.
checklist.done: the bulletin log shows an unbroken weekly review trail and every relevant bulletin has a saved capture and a relevance call.

checklist.step: Load the weekly transaction cutoff schedule for the reinsurance year
actions: Download the current M13/Appendix III transaction cutoff schedule from the RMA site (or pull it from the eDAS announcements screen after eAuth login).

Enter all 52 weekly cutoff dates for the reinsurance year into the calendar, each tagged 'Appendix III weekly submission' with the rule 'records accepted no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week'.
Cross-check the first four cutoffs against the dates PASS actually enforced last month, asking Data Management to confirm from their acceptance receipts.
Version the schedule so a mid-year RMA change is a visible diff, not a silent overwrite.
checklist.done: all weekly cutoffs for the reinsurance year are calendared, verified against actual PASS acceptances, and versioned.

checklist.step: Calendar the April 1 Plan of Operations with backed-off internal milestones
actions: Enter the statutory deadline: complete Plan of Operations to FCIC by April 1 preceding the reinsurance year, per 2026 SRA Section IV(f)(2) and Appendix II.

Back off internal milestones and enter each: Appendix II content owners' drafts due March 1, CFO sign-off of estimated retained premium and fund designations by March 15, final internal approval by March 25.

Attach the Appendix II content checklist (estimated retained premium, fund designations, financial and operational resources, internal controls, risk-scenario assessment, service-provider information) to the calendar entry.
Note on the entry that an incomplete Plan is not accepted by FCIC, so partial submission does not stop the clock.
checklist.done: the April 1 deadline and its three backed-off internal milestones are calendared with the Appendix II content checklist attached.

checklist.step: Calendar the monthly accounting and escrow reporting deadlines
actions: From Appendix III, list each monthly accounting report and escrow-related submission with its due-day rule.
Enter 12 monthly entries per report into the calendar, owner set to the Controller's team contact.
Confirm with the Reinsurance Accountant which reports the company actually owes given its fund designations, and mark the rest 'not applicable — rechecked annually'.
Record the confirmation email in the evidence folder.
checklist.done: every applicable monthly report is calendared for all 12 months with a confirmed owner.

checklist.step: Register ad-hoc RMA data calls within 3 business days of receipt
actions: On receipt of any RMA data call (bulletin, memorandum or direct email from the RMA regional or compliance office), create a calendar entry within 3 business days carrying the RMA reference, receipt date, due date and demanded data set.
Forward the request the same day to the Data Quality Manager for feasibility and to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for ownership.
Where the due date is unclear, email the issuing RMA contact for confirmation and log the question and answer on the entry.
Acknowledge receipt to RMA where the request asks for acknowledgment.
checklist.done: every data call is calendared within 3 business days with reference, due date, data set and named owner.

checklist.step: Assign a named owner and backup to every calendared obligation
actions: Walk the calendar and set an accountable owner and a backup on every entry: weekly submissions to Data Management, Plan of Operations to Regulatory Reporting, monthly accounting to the Controller's team, privacy-triggered items to the Privacy Officer.
Reject any entry owned by a mailbox or a team name without a person attached.
Publish the ownership matrix to the owners and their managers and collect a read acknowledgment.
Re-run the walk whenever an owner leaves or changes role.
checklist.done: no calendar entry lacks a named owner and backup, and the ownership matrix is acknowledged.

checklist.step: Configure the reminder ladder on every deadline
actions: Set alerts at T-10, T-5 and T-1 business days on every weekly and monthly entry, delivered to the owner, the backup and the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Set T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts on the April 1 Plan of Operations and on any data call with more than 30 days' notice.
Send a test alert for one entry in each series and confirm all three recipients received it.
Screenshot the reminder configuration into the evidence folder.
checklist.done: every entry has the full reminder ladder, a test alert was received by all recipients, and the configuration is captured.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar against last reinsurance year's actual submissions
actions: Pull last year's submission receipts and acceptance confirmations from the submission archive held by the Records Manager.
Match each historical submission type to a current calendar entry; any historical submission with no current entry is a candidate gap.
Investigate each gap with the Regulatory Reporting Manager: either the obligation ended (record the citation) or the calendar is missing it (add it).
File the reconciliation worksheet in the evidence folder.
checklist.done: every prior-year submission type maps to a current entry or a documented obligation-ended citation.

checklist.step: Publish the calendar to every contributing team
actions: Publish a read-only view of the calendar to the crop reporting SharePoint site visible to Data Management, Claims, Actuarial, the Controller's team and the Privacy Office.
Walk the calendar in the monthly crop-reporting operations meeting and capture disputes about dates or ownership as change requests.
Notify all owners by email when the reinsurance-year rollover version is published each July.
Keep the published view pointed at the live calendar, never a static copy.
checklist.done: contributing teams work from the single published live view and the rollover notice went to all owners.

checklist.step: Run change control when RMA moves a cutoff or issues a revised schedule
actions: On any bulletin or eDAS announcement changing a date, open a calendar change request quoting the RMA source and the old and new dates.
Apply the change, re-run the reminder ladder on the moved entry, and notify the owner and backup the same day.
Where a cutoff moves earlier, check with the Data Quality Manager that the extract pipeline can still land 2 business days ahead of it.
Close the change request with the bulletin capture attached.
checklist.done: every date change traces to a quoted RMA source, reminders were rebuilt, and affected owners were notified same-day.

checklist.step: Spot-check calendar completeness against the bulletin log monthly
actions: Once a month, take every bulletin logged as 'reporting impact' in the last 31 days and verify a matching calendar entry or change request exists.
Verify the entry landed within 3 business days of the bulletin issue date by comparing the two timestamps.
Record the check (date, items verified, gaps) in the monthly QC note.
Open an exception for any gap found.
checklist.done: the monthly QC note shows every impactful bulletin matched to a timely calendar entry, or exceptions raised.

checklist.step: Log every miss or near-miss as an exception with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any deadline missed, any data call calendared late, and any reminder that failed to fire, stating the obligation, the SRA citation and the business impact.
Assign a root cause (bulletin not read, mailbox coverage gap, reminder misconfigured, owner absent) and a named remediation owner.
For an actual missed RMA submission, notify Head of Compliance the same day and let Regulatory Counsel steer any proactive contact with RMA.
Track the fix to closure and reference the issue id on the calendar entry.
checklist.done: every miss and near-miss has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation and closure evidence.

checklist.step: Archive the calendar and its evidence for the retention period
actions: At each quarter end, export the calendar (entries, owners, reminder configs, change log) and file it in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C17/<reinsurance year>.
File alongside it the quarter's bulletin captures, QC notes and reconciliation worksheets.
Apply the retention label: 3 years after the end of the reinsurance year, extended on any FCIC review or litigation hold.
Confirm the archive is retrievable by obligation name and RMA bulletin number.
checklist.done: the quarterly export and its evidence are filed, retention-labelled, and retrievable by obligation and bulletin number.

testing.step: Build the obligation population from RMA sources, not from the calendar
actions: Independently list the reinsurance year's obligations from the executed 2026 SRA (Sections III/IV, Appendices II and III) and from the rma.usda.gov bulletin archive for the period.
Add every data call found in the shared Regulatory Reporting mailbox and in RMA correspondence held by the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Record the population count and sources in the workpaper before looking at the team's calendar.
testing.done: an independently built obligation population exists with documented sources and counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the independent population to the calendar
actions: Match every population row to a calendar entry on obligation name, due date and owner.
List as exceptions: population rows with no entry, entries created more than 3 business days after the bulletin issue date, and entries with no named owner or backup.
Reconcile the entry count both ways — calendar entries with no population source are checked for validity too.
testing.done: every population row matches a timely, owned calendar entry or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of calendar entries
actions: Take 100% of annual obligations (Plan of Operations, annual settlement items) plus a seeded random sample of 8 weekly cutoffs, 4 monthly reports and every ad-hoc data call in the period.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
File the sample list in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all annual items and every data call is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the deadline lookup for each sampled entry
actions: For each sampled entry, independently re-derive the due date from the SRA text, the M13 cutoff schedule or the issuing bulletin without reading the calendar's citation first.
Compare the re-derived date and citation to the calendar entry; any difference, including a right date with a wrong citation, is an exception.
Capture the source page (bulletin PDF or SRA extract) into the workpaper for each re-performance.
testing.done: each sampled entry has an independent re-derived date, a comparison note and a captured source.

testing.step: Verify the reminder ladder actually fired
actions: For 5 sampled entries with past due dates, pull the reminder delivery logs and confirm T-10/T-5/T-1 alerts fired to owner, backup and manager.
Screenshot the configuration and the delivery evidence into the workpaper.
Treat a configured-but-unfired reminder as a control failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: reminder firing is evidenced for the sampled past entries, or failures are logged.

testing.step: Trace sampled data calls from receipt to calendar within 3 business days
actions: For every ad-hoc data call in the sample, take the receipt timestamp from the mailbox or RMA letter and the creation timestamp of the calendar entry.
Compute the gap in business days and flag anything over 3 as an exception.
Confirm the entry carries the RMA reference and demanded data set as received.
testing.done: every sampled data call shows a computed receipt-to-entry gap within 3 business days, or an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the April 1 back-off milestones
actions: Recompute the Plan of Operations internal milestones from the April 1 statutory date and compare to the calendared March 1/March 15/March 25 milestones.

Verify the Appendix II content checklist attached to the entry names all required elements (estimated retained premium, fund designations, resources, internal controls, risk-scenario assessment, service providers).
Flag any milestone that leaves less than 5 business days of final-approval buffer before April 1.
testing.done: the milestone maths reconciles and the Appendix II checklist is complete, or gaps are logged.

testing.step: Check actual submissions met the calendared dates
actions: For each sampled entry with a past due date, pull the submission receipt or PASS acceptance confirmation from the submission archive.
Compare the actual submission timestamp to the calendared deadline; a submission after the weekly transaction cutoff or after April 1 is a reportable exception.
Cross-note any miss against the exception log to check it was self-identified.
testing.done: every sampled past deadline shows an on-time receipt, or a miss that was self-identified and logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the obligation, the SRA/bulletin citation and the impact.
Assign root cause (bulletin missed, late entry, reminder failure, owner gap) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next test cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-uncalendared-obligations threshold and write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who neither maintains the calendar nor owns any entry — sign the workpaper.
Report results to Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C17.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns extraction and validation of Appendix III record sets for FCIC submission; escalation to Chief Data Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Section IV(d) and Appendix III (M13 Data Acceptance System Handbook) record layouts, plus 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 14 for claim-data completeness; layouts re-verified against the current Appendix III release before each reinsurance year

In-scope processes.value: Extraction of crop policy, acreage/yield, premium and loss records from the policy administration and claims platforms, mapping to Appendix III record types, and pre-submission validation ahead of each weekly PASS transaction cutoff

In-scope systems.value: Source data from Policy Administration Platform and Claims Platform staged in the enterprise data warehouse; edit checks mirror the RMA eDAS/PASS acceptance edits

Compliance procedure documented.value: FCIC Data Extraction & Validation Procedure — field mapping to Appendix III record types (policy, acreage/yield, premium, loss line), Actuarial Data Master (ADM) reference checks, local edit run, validation report issuance

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Data Officer; re-approved on every Appendix III layout change published by RMA and at each reinsurance-year rollover

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Validated extract must be handed to Regulatory Reporting at least 2 business days before the weekly transaction cutoff; annual layout refresh completed before July 1; FCIC-directed corrections completed within 45 days of FCIC notice

Deadline reminders configured.value: Pipeline SLA alerts fire when the weekly extract has not completed by T-3 business days before cutoff, escalating to the Data Quality Manager at T-2

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per-extract validation reports, mapping specs, ADM reference versions and reconciliation worksheets retained 3 years after the end of the reinsurance year per 2026 SRA Appendix III

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every failed edit, mapping defect and count mismatch logged as a data-quality issue with severity, disposition and fix release

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CDO signs off remediation of any defect that reached an FCIC submission or breached the 45-day correction window

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All weekly extract batches produced in the quarter for PASS submission, by record type, plus every crop claim paid in the quarter for section 14 completeness testing

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Extract-to-source reconciliation must tie to zero unexplained differences; PASS first-pass acceptance rate at or above 99%; any claim record missing a section 14 mandatory element is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per weekly data call cycle; test runs quarterly over the quarter's batches with 100% coverage of any batch that missed cutoff

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or run any sampled extract or authored the mapping spec

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly extraction-validation test workpaper (population, reconciliation, sample, re-performed edits, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C18

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Mapping spec with Appendix III citations, validation reports per batch and PASS acceptance statistics, producible to an RMA compliance reviewer within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Data Quality Manager supports RMA data inquiries with the Regulatory Reporting Manager as the RMA-facing contact; Regulatory Counsel clears any response describing a data defect

checklist.step: Maintain the field-level mapping spec against the current Appendix III layouts
actions: Download the current Appendix III/M13 record layouts for the reinsurance year from the RMA site and diff them against last year's version, listing every added, removed or redefined field.

Update the mapping spec so every Appendix III field maps to a named source column in the Policy Administration Platform or Claims Platform, with transformation logic written out (code translations, unit conversions, date formats).
Mark every mandatory field and its permissible-value set exactly as the layout defines them.
Have the Data Quality Manager approve the updated spec before the first extract of the reinsurance year runs.
checklist.done: the mapping spec covers every current Appendix III field with a named source, transformation and mandatory flag, and is approved.

checklist.step: Refresh the RMA reference data before each extract cycle
actions: Download the current Actuarial Data Master (ADM) release from RMA and load the crop, county, practice, type and insurance-plan code tables into the reference data store.
Record the ADM release identifier used for the cycle so every validated record ties to a specific reference version.
Diff the new release against the prior one and notify the Data Quality Analyst of code changes that touch in-force policies.
Reject any extract run pointed at a stale ADM release.
checklist.done: the cycle runs against a recorded current ADM release and code changes were communicated.

checklist.step: Run the weekly extract from the source platforms
actions: Trigger the scheduled extract DAG that pulls new and changed policy, acreage/yield, premium and loss records since the last accepted batch from the Policy Administration Platform and Claims Platform.
Verify the DAG completed with zero task failures and record the batch id, record counts per Appendix III record type and the extraction window timestamps.
Land the raw extract in the warehouse staging schema, immutable and batch-stamped.
Alert the Data Quality Manager immediately if the run has not completed by T-3 business days before the weekly transaction cutoff.
checklist.done: a batch-stamped extract with per-record-type counts sits in staging at least 3 business days before cutoff.

checklist.step: Reconcile extract counts and amounts back to the source systems
actions: Run the reconciliation queries comparing extract record counts, total premium and total indemnity per county/crop against the source platform's own period totals.
Investigate every difference to a named cause (timing, cancelled policy, correction record) and record it on the reconciliation worksheet.
Refuse to pass the batch forward while any unexplained difference remains.
File the signed worksheet against the batch id.
checklist.done: counts, premium and indemnity tie to source with every difference explained on a filed worksheet.

checklist.step: Validate mandatory fields and code values against the layouts and ADM
actions: Run the rule pack that checks every mandatory Appendix III field is populated and every coded field (crop, county, practice, type, plan, unit structure) resolves against the loaded ADM release.
Check cross-field logic: acreage dates within the crop year, share percentages between 0 and 1, liability = quantity x price x share within rounding tolerance.
Write failures to the data-quality issue queue with record key, rule id and failed value.
Publish the pass/fail statistics per record type on the batch dashboard.
checklist.done: the rule pack ran on the full batch and every failure is queued with record key and rule id.

checklist.step: Validate claim records for section 14 completeness before they leave the building
actions: For every loss record in the batch, verify the underlying claim was made on the company form meeting FCIC standards and that the record carries all elements needed to pay the indemnity per 7 CFR 457.8 section 14: cause of loss code, date of damage, unit, appraised/harvested production, and adjuster identifier.
Cross-check the adjuster identifier against the loss-adjuster roster maintained under Appendix IV so no claim carries an unqualified adjuster.
Queue any loss record with a missing element back to the Claims Director / Manager for completion rather than defaulting values.
Log each queued record in the data-quality tool with the missing element named.
checklist.done: every loss record either carries all section 14 elements and a rostered adjuster id, or is queued back to Claims by name.

checklist.step: Run the local mirror of the eDAS/PASS acceptance edits
actions: Execute the pre-submission edit package that mirrors the published RMA eDAS/PASS edits for the reinsurance year against the validated batch.
Compare the local edit outcomes with last cycle's actual PASS responses and flag any edit the mirror no longer predicts correctly for maintenance.
Hold back individual records that fail the mirror rather than failing the whole batch, listing each held record with its edit code.
Hand the held-record list to the Data Quality Analyst for correction in the source system.
checklist.done: the batch passed the local edit mirror, held records are listed with edit codes, and mirror drift is flagged.

checklist.step: Produce and sign the batch validation report
actions: Compile the validation report for the batch: record counts per type, reconciliation result, rule-pack pass rates, section 14 completeness result, local edit result, held records and the ADM release used.
State the disposition — cleared for submission, cleared with held records, or blocked — and the reason.
Sign and date the report and file it against the batch id in the evidence folder.
Send the report to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and the Data Quality Manager.
checklist.done: a signed validation report with a stated disposition is filed and delivered before hand-off.

checklist.step: Hand the cleared batch to Regulatory Reporting ahead of the cutoff
actions: Release the cleared batch file set to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst no later than 2 business days before the weekly transaction cutoff, referencing the batch id and validation report.
Confirm receipt in writing and record the hand-off timestamp on the batch record.
Where the batch cannot be cleared in time, notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager and Head of Compliance before the cutoff, never after it.
Track partial submissions (cleared records only) so held records join the next weekly cycle.
checklist.done: the cleared batch is with Regulatory Reporting 2 business days pre-cutoff with a written receipt, or the miss was escalated pre-cutoff.

checklist.step: Correct source data for failed records in the system of record
actions: Work the correction queue: open each failed policy/acreage record in the Policy Administration Platform, correct the named field at source, and note the data-quality issue id on the change.
Never patch the extract file directly — corrections happen only in the system of record so the next extract picks them up.
Confirm with the Data Quality Analyst that the corrected record passes revalidation in the next cycle.
Close the data-quality issue with the correction reference.
checklist.done: every failed record is corrected at source, revalidated clean, and its issue closed with a reference.

checklist.step: Complete FCIC-directed corrections within the 45-day window
actions: When FCIC/RMA notifies the company of data errors, log the notice date and compute the correction deadline at 45 days from FCIC notice.
Assign each noticed error to a correction owner and track daily against the 45-day clock, escalating to the Chief Data Officer at day 30 if open.
Resubmit corrected records through the normal weekly cycle and confirm PASS acceptance before the deadline.
File the FCIC notice, correction evidence and acceptance confirmations together.
checklist.done: every FCIC-noticed error is corrected and accepted within 45 days of FCIC notice, with the clock evidenced.

checklist.step: Protect PII within the extraction pipeline
actions: Verify the staging schemas holding producer SSN/EIN and other Protected Information are access-restricted to the named pipeline roles, checking the grants list against the approved access matrix.
Confirm masked views are used for all development and troubleshooting work on the extract.
Report any unauthorized access or suspected loss of Protected Information immediately to the Privacy Officer for the one-hour FCIC report clock under Appendix III.
Record the quarterly access review result in the privacy evidence folder.
checklist.done: staging access matches the approved matrix, dev work uses masked views, and the access review is recorded.

checklist.step: Version and regression-test the pipeline on every change
actions: Keep mapping code, rule packs and the edit mirror in the source repository with peer-reviewed pull requests — no direct production edits.
Run the regression suite (golden-batch comparison against known-accepted output) on every merge and block deployment on failure.
Tag the deployed version on each batch record so any output traces to exact code.
Record Appendix III layout-change releases as their own tagged versions.
checklist.done: every pipeline change is peer-reviewed, regression-tested and version-tagged onto the batches it produced.

checklist.step: Review validation metrics monthly and tune the rule pack
actions: Review the monthly dashboard: first-pass PASS acceptance rate, top 10 edit failures by code, correction cycle time and 45-day clock performance.
Commission rule-pack additions for any PASS rejection reason the local mirror failed to predict twice in the month.
Share the metrics with the Regulatory Reporting Manager and Chief Data Officer.
Minute agreed actions and owners.
checklist.done: monthly metrics are reviewed, mirror gaps are turned into rules, and actions are minuted with owners.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle's validation evidence
actions: File each batch's validation report, reconciliation worksheet, held-record list and hand-off receipt in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C18/<reinsurance year>/<batch id>.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label.
Verify retrievability by batch id and by week-ending date.
Confirm the Records Manager's index picked up the new folder.
checklist.done: the batch evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by batch id and week.

testing.step: Build the population of extract batches and paid claims for the quarter
actions: List every extract batch produced in the quarter from the pipeline run log, with record counts per Appendix III record type.
Independently pull the quarter's paid crop claims from the Claims Platform for the section 14 completeness test.
Reconcile the batch list to the hand-off receipts held by Regulatory Reporting and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the batch and claim populations are built, reconciled to receipts, and counted in the workpaper.

testing.step: Reconcile a re-run of the source totals to the submitted extracts
actions: For 3 selected weeks, independently re-run the source-system totals (record counts, premium, indemnity by county/crop) and compare to the batch that was submitted.
Verify each difference matches an explanation on the team's reconciliation worksheet.
Treat any unexplained difference as an exception regardless of size.
testing.done: re-run totals tie to submitted batches with every difference matching a documented explanation.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of records and batches
actions: Select a seeded random sample of 25 records per record type across the quarter's batches, plus 100% of any batch that missed the cutoff or was blocked.
Select 25 paid claims at random for section 14 completeness re-testing.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample exists covering all record types, blocked batches and 25 paid claims.

testing.step: Re-perform the mapping for sampled records field by field
actions: For each sampled record, open the source policy or claim in the source platform and independently derive each Appendix III field value using the mapping spec.
Compare to the value actually submitted; any mismatch, including formatting that breaches the layout, is an exception.
Verify coded fields resolve against the ADM release recorded for that batch, not the current release.
testing.done: every sampled record's submitted values reconcile field-by-field to source under the batch's ADM release.

testing.step: Re-test section 14 completeness on the sampled claims
actions: Open each sampled claim and verify it was taken on the company form meeting FCIC standards and contains every element needed to pay the indemnity: cause of loss, date of damage, unit identification, production counts and adjuster identifier.
Check the adjuster identifier against the Appendix IV training roster in force at the adjustment date.
List any claim paid despite a missing element as a fail with the element named.
testing.done: each sampled claim demonstrates full section 14 content and a rostered adjuster, or is listed as a fail.

testing.step: Re-run the edit rule pack on a sampled batch and compare outcomes
actions: Re-execute the validation rule pack and local edit mirror against one sampled batch's staged data.
Compare failures found with the failures recorded on the original validation report — new failures mean the pack changed or was not run as claimed.
Verify the batch's stated disposition (cleared/held/blocked) follows from the recorded results.
testing.done: the re-run reproduces the recorded edit results and the disposition follows from them.

testing.step: Trace held and corrected records through to accepted resubmission
actions: Take 10 held records from the quarter and trace each: data-quality issue, source-system correction, revalidation, resubmission batch and PASS acceptance.
Confirm corrections were made in the system of record, not patched in the extract file, by inspecting the source change history.
Flag any record still uncorrected after two weekly cycles.
testing.done: sampled held records trace end-to-end to source-corrected, accepted resubmissions.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day FCIC correction clocks
actions: For every FCIC-noticed error in the quarter, recompute the deadline as FCIC notice date plus 45 days and compare to the acceptance date of the corrected record.
Verify the day-30 escalation to the Chief Data Officer fired for any item still open at day 30.
Any correction accepted after day 45 is a reportable compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: all noticed errors closed within 45 days with escalations evidenced, or breaches are reported.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception citing batch id or claim number, the Appendix III or section 14 requirement breached, and the impact.
Assign root cause (mapping defect, stale ADM, rule gap, source data entry, claims form gap) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the reconciliation, acceptance-rate and section 14 results against the thresholds (zero unexplained differences, 99% first-pass acceptance, zero missing mandatory claim elements).
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — who built or ran none of the sampled extracts — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Chief Data Officer and Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper under REG-056/C18.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion against thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain USDA eAuthentication credentials and RMA application access
actions: Keep at least two active submitters with verified USDA eAuth accounts linked to the company's RMA application roles (eDAS/PASS upload and Plan of Operations), so a single absence cannot block a cutoff.
Review the RMA access roster quarterly with the Access Management Analyst; remove leavers within 5 business days and record the review.
Test both submitters' eAuth logins in the first week of each quarter and log the result.
Track eAuth password/credential expiry dates on the team calendar so no expiry lands in a cutoff week.
checklist.done: two verified submitters hold working eAuth access, the roster review is recorded, and no credential expires in a cutoff week.

checklist.step: Receive the cleared batch and verify it is submission-ready
actions: Accept the batch hand-off from the Data Quality Manager with its signed validation report, at least 2 business days before the weekly transaction cutoff.
Check the report disposition reads 'cleared for submission' (or 'cleared with held records' with the held list attached) and that the batch id and record counts match the file set.
Refuse any batch without a signed validation report — send it back rather than submitting on trust.
Log the receipt timestamp in the submission log.
checklist.done: the batch is logged as received with a matching signed validation report and a cleared disposition.

checklist.step: Upload the weekly batch to RMA before the cutoff
actions: Log in through USDA eAuthentication and open the RMA eDAS/PASS submission function for the company code.
Upload the batch file set in the Appendix III format, verifying the portal echoes the correct reinsurance year, company code and record counts before confirming.
Submit no later than 1 business day before the transaction cutoff date for the week; treat cutoff day itself as contingency only.
Record the submission timestamp and portal-assigned identifiers in the submission log immediately.
checklist.done: the batch is uploaded with matching counts and the submission timestamp precedes the weekly cutoff with a day in hand.

checklist.step: Capture the acceptance receipt and reconcile accepted counts
actions: After PASS processing, retrieve the acceptance/processing report and save it as PDF named <batch-id>-receipt-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf in the evidence repository.
Reconcile accepted record counts per type against the submitted counts; pass any rejected-record detail to the Data Quality Manager the same day for the C20 correction process.
Update the submission log entry with accepted, rejected and pending counts.
Alert the Regulatory Reporting Manager if the receipt is not available within the portal's normal processing window.
checklist.done: a saved receipt reconciles to the submission, rejects are handed to Data Management same-day, and the log is updated.

checklist.step: Kick off the Plan of Operations assembly in January
actions: Open the Plan of Operations case in January with the Appendix II content checklist as tasks: estimated retained premium, fund designations, financial and operational resources, internal controls description, risk-scenario assessment and service-provider information.

Assign each content section to its owner — retained premium and fund designations to the Capital Management Manager and CFO's team, internal controls to Compliance, service providers to the Procurement Manager — with drafts due March 1.
Circulate last year's accepted Plan and any RMA feedback on it as the drafting baseline.
Track task status weekly and escalate slipping sections at the March 1 gate.
checklist.done: the case is open with every Appendix II section owned, baselined and due March 1.

checklist.step: Run the Appendix II completeness gate before submission
actions: Check every Appendix II element against the assembled package line by line — FCIC does not accept an incomplete Plan, so a missing exhibit costs the deadline, not just a follow-up.
Verify the estimated retained premium and fund designations carry CFO sign-off dated by March 15.
Have a second reader who did not assemble the package repeat the completeness check independently.
Record both checks on the case with names and dates.
checklist.done: two independent completeness checks confirm every Appendix II element is present with CFO sign-off in place.

checklist.step: Submit the complete Plan of Operations by April 1
actions: Log in through USDA eAuthentication, open the RMA Plan of Operations application, and enter or upload each Appendix II section for the coming reinsurance year.
Target internal submission by March 25 so a portal problem or FCIC completeness query still leaves runway before April 1.
Capture the portal confirmation screen and any FCIC acknowledgment email and file both in the evidence repository.
Record the submission timestamp on the case and notify the CFO and Head of Compliance of completion.
checklist.done: the complete Plan is submitted with confirmation captured and the timestamp is on or before April 1 with the March 25 target met or the variance explained.

checklist.step: Respond to FCIC completeness or clarification queries on the Plan
actions: Log any FCIC query on the Plan the day it arrives, with the response due date FCIC states.
Route the question to the owning content section's author and have Regulatory Counsel clear the response before it goes back.
Submit the response through the same RMA portal thread and capture the confirmation.
Track the query to FCIC's written acceptance of the Plan.
checklist.done: every FCIC query is logged, answered through the portal by its due date with counsel clearance, and traced to acceptance.

checklist.step: Mirror every submission into the internal submission log
actions: Maintain one log row per submission: obligation, batch id or Plan year, cutoff/deadline date, submission timestamp, portal identifier, receipt reference and accepted/rejected counts.
Enter the row the day of submission, not in arrears.
Link the row to the receipt PDF in the evidence repository.
Leave no row without a receipt reference for more than 3 business days.
checklist.done: the log carries a same-day row with linked receipt for every submission, with no receipt gaps over 3 business days.

checklist.step: Run the noon-on-cutoff-day alarm drill
actions: Keep a standing noon check on every cutoff day: if the week's batch shows unsubmitted, phone — not email — the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and the Data Quality Manager.
If the batch cannot be submitted before the cutoff, notify Head of Compliance before the cutoff passes and record the decision trail.
Rehearse the fallback path (second submitter, alternate workstation, RMA help desk contact) once each quarter and log the drill.
Keep the RMA help desk number and the company's RMA regional office contact on the procedure sheet.
checklist.done: the noon check runs every cutoff day, the fallback drill is logged quarterly, and any at-risk cutoff was escalated before it passed.

checklist.step: Handle portal outages and RMA-side failures defensively
actions: On any eDAS/PASS error or outage, screenshot the error with its timestamp immediately and open a ticket with the RMA help desk, recording the ticket number.
Retry on the documented schedule and keep every attempt's timestamp in the log.
If the outage threatens the cutoff, have the Regulatory Reporting Manager email the RMA regional office before the cutoff stating the batch is ready and blocked by the outage, attaching evidence.
File the outage evidence with the eventual receipt so the record shows the company was ready on time.
checklist.done: every outage has timestamped evidence, an RMA ticket, a pre-cutoff notification where needed, and a closing receipt.

checklist.step: Verify monthly accounting submissions ride the same discipline
actions: For each monthly Appendix III accounting report, collect the prepared report from the Reinsurance Accountant with its reviewer sign-off.
Submit through the required RMA channel by the calendared date and capture the confirmation.
Log the submission in the same submission log with receipt linked.
Chase the Controller's team at T-5 business days if the prepared report has not arrived.
checklist.done: monthly reports are submitted on time with sign-off, receipts captured and log rows written.

checklist.step: Brief backups and document the submission runbook
actions: Keep the submission runbook current on the team wiki: eAuth login path, portal screens, file naming, receipt capture, escalation contacts and the outage playbook.
Walk the backup submitter through a live weekly submission at least twice a year and record the walkthroughs.
Update the runbook within 5 business days of any RMA portal change.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Analyst peer-review each update.
checklist.done: the runbook is current, backup walkthroughs are recorded twice yearly, and portal changes are reflected within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Review submission timeliness monthly
actions: Review the monthly view of submission timestamps versus cutoffs: days-early distribution, any same-day submissions and any misses.
Investigate every same-day submission as a near-miss with the analyst and record the cause.
Report the month's timeliness to Head of Compliance with the near-miss causes.
Feed recurring causes into the procedure or the C17 reminder ladder.
checklist.done: monthly timeliness is reviewed, near-misses carry causes, and recurring causes changed the procedure.

checklist.step: Archive submission evidence for the retention period
actions: File all receipts, confirmation screens, the Plan of Operations package and FCIC acceptance correspondence under REG-056/C19/<reinsurance year> in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label, extended on FCIC review or litigation hold.
Verify retrieval by batch id, week-ending date and Plan year.
Hand the index to the Records Manager for the C21 archive.
checklist.done: all submission evidence is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable; the index is with Records Management.

testing.step: Build the population of required submissions for the year
actions: Derive the expected submission set independently: 52 weekly cutoffs from the M13 schedule, 12 monthly reports and the April 1 Plan of Operations.
Pull the actual submission log rows for the same period.
Record both counts in the workpaper before reconciling.
testing.done: expected and actual submission populations are built independently and counted.

testing.step: Reconcile expected submissions to logged submissions
actions: Match every expected submission to a log row; a cutoff week with no log row is an automatic exception.
Match every log row to a linked acceptance receipt; a row without a receipt is an exception.
Check the log rows were written same-day by comparing row creation timestamps to submission timestamps.
testing.done: every expected submission matches a same-day log row with a linked receipt, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take the Plan of Operations (100%), all misses and same-day submissions (100%), plus a seeded random 8 weekly and 3 monthly submissions.
Record seed, population and selection date for reproducibility.
File the sample list in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the Plan, all near-misses and a random weekly/monthly spread is documented.

testing.step: Trace sampled weekly submissions to PASS receipts and recompute timeliness
actions: Open each sampled receipt PDF and read the portal timestamp and identifiers directly from the receipt, not the log.
Recompute timeliness: submission timestamp versus the M13 transaction cutoff date for that week.
Verify accepted counts on the receipt reconcile to the batch validation report counts.
Any submission after the cutoff is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: sampled receipts prove pre-cutoff submission with counts reconciling to validation reports.

testing.step: Re-verify the Plan of Operations completeness and April 1 timing
actions: Open the submitted Plan package and check every Appendix II element is present: estimated retained premium, fund designations, resources, internal controls, risk-scenario assessment, service-provider information.
Verify the CFO sign-off on retained premium and fund designations pre-dates submission.
Read the portal confirmation timestamp and confirm it is on or before April 1; verify any FCIC completeness query was answered by its due date.
Confirm FCIC's written acceptance is on file.
testing.done: the Plan traces to a complete, signed-off, timely submission with FCIC acceptance evidenced.

testing.step: Verify credential and access controls held during the period
actions: Pull the RMA/eAuth access roster and compare against HR leaver records for the period; any leaver retaining access past 5 business days is an exception.
Verify two active submitters existed throughout, including across the April window.
Check the quarterly login tests and access reviews were recorded.
testing.done: access reviews, dual-submitter coverage and leaver removals are evidenced for the whole period.

testing.step: Test the outage and escalation trail on any disrupted cutoff
actions: For any week the log shows portal errors or outage, verify timestamped screenshots, the RMA help desk ticket number and the pre-cutoff notification to the RMA regional office where the cutoff was at risk.
Verify Head of Compliance was notified before, not after, any cutoff that passed unsubmitted.
Confirm the quarterly fallback drills were logged.
testing.done: every disruption shows a complete contemporaneous evidence trail and pre-cutoff escalation.

testing.step: Reconcile rejected records hand-offs to the correction process
actions: For sampled receipts showing rejected records, verify the reject detail reached the Data Quality Manager the same day.
Trace two rejects into the C20 exception log to confirm the hand-off actually starts the correction clock.
Flag any reject that sat unrouted for more than one business day.
testing.done: sampled rejects were handed off same-day and appear in the correction process log.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the submission, cutoff date, citation (Appendix II/III) and impact.
Assign root cause (late hand-off, credential gap, portal outage handling, log discipline) with a named owner and date.
Open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any post-cutoff submission.
Carry open items into the next test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and — for breaches — a counsel-led self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the timeliness results against the zero-late threshold and the Plan's first-submission acceptance requirement.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references and have the independent reviewer, who executed no sampled submission, sign.
Report to Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C19.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Pull the PASS processing report the day it is available
actions: After each weekly submission, retrieve the PASS/eDAS processing and rejection report through the RMA portal session opened by the Regulatory Reporting Analyst, or from the same-day hand-off under C19.
Save the report against the batch id and record the retrieval timestamp.
Diff the rejected-record count against the acceptance receipt totals to confirm nothing on the report was missed.
Alert the Data Quality Manager if the report is unavailable within the portal's normal processing window.
checklist.done: each week's processing report is saved, timestamped, and its reject count reconciles to the acceptance receipt.

checklist.step: Load every rejected record into the exception log within 1 business day
actions: Create one exception-log entry per rejected or edit-failed record carrying: record key, Appendix III record type, edit code and edit message exactly as PASS returned them, batch id and reject date.
Set the target resubmission date to the next weekly transaction cutoff on every entry at creation.
Confirm the log entry count equals the processing report's reject count before closing the intake.
Timestamp intake completion — the 1-business-day clock is measured from the processing report retrieval.
checklist.done: log entries equal the report's reject count, each carries the verbatim edit code, and intake closed within 1 business day.

checklist.step: Triage each edit code to a root-cause category and owner
actions: Look up each edit code in the current-year Appendix III edit specification and classify the failure: source data entry, mapping/transformation defect, stale ADM reference, RMA-side reference change, or timing (record out of sequence).
Route source data entry failures to the Policy Administration Analyst or the Claims team; mapping and reference failures to the Data Engineer.
Set severity: blocking (record cannot pay or report without it) versus standard.
Record category, owner and severity on every log entry.
checklist.done: every entry carries an edit-spec-based category, a named correction owner and a severity.

checklist.step: Correct source-data failures in the system of record
actions: Open each routed record in the Policy Administration Platform (or hand claims-side records to the Claims Analyst for the Claims Platform), correct the specific field the edit code names, and reference the exception-log id on the change.
Where the correct value needs producer input (e.g. acreage or share discrepancies), request it through the agency channel and log the request date on the entry.
Never force a value simply to clear the edit — an edit cleared with wrong data is a worse failure than a reject.
Mark the entry 'corrected — awaiting resubmission' with the correction timestamp.
checklist.done: each routed record is corrected at source with the log id referenced, or shows a dated producer-input request.

checklist.step: Fix mapping and reference-data defects with a versioned release
actions: For mapping or transformation defects, fix the pipeline code via a peer-reviewed pull request, run the regression suite, and tag the release on the exception entries it resolves.
For stale-reference failures, reload the current ADM release and re-derive the affected records.
Sweep the full book for other records carrying the same defect — not just the rejected ones — and queue them for correction in the same release.
Record the sweep result (records found and corrected) on the log entries.
checklist.done: the defect is fixed in a tagged, tested release and the full-book sweep result is recorded.

checklist.step: Resubmit corrected records at the next weekly cutoff
actions: Include every 'corrected — awaiting resubmission' record in the next weekly batch handed to Regulatory Reporting under the C18/C19 cycle, flagged as resubmissions with their exception-log ids.
Verify each resubmitted record passes the local edit mirror before it goes into the batch.
After the batch's PASS receipt arrives, mark each accepted record's log entry 'closed — accepted' with the acceptance date and receipt reference.
Reopen and re-triage any record PASS rejects a second time, flagging it as a repeat rejection.
checklist.done: corrected records rode the next cutoff, acceptances are closed with receipt references, and repeats are flagged.

checklist.step: Escalate repeat rejections and aged exceptions
actions: Review the aging view weekly: entries open 3, 7 and 14 days trigger the ladder — analyst chase, manager review, then Chief Data Officer notification at 14 days.
Treat any second rejection of the same record for the same edit code as a defect in the correction process itself and assign it to the Data Engineer for root-cause analysis.
Minute the weekly review with entry counts by age band and the actions taken.
Sign closure on every entry that aged past 14 days.
checklist.done: the weekly aging review is minuted, repeats have root-cause assignments, and 14-day items carry manager sign-off.

checklist.step: Run the 45-day clock on FCIC-directed corrections
actions: When RMA/FCIC issues an error notice or directed correction, open a tracker issue the same day recording the FCIC notice date and computing the deadline at 45 days from FCIC notice.
Break the notice into record-level exception entries linked to the tracker issue.
Watch the clock alerts at day 20, day 30 (escalate to Chief Data Officer) and day 40 (escalate to Head of Compliance).
Close the issue only when every linked record shows PASS acceptance inside the window, and file the FCIC notice with the acceptance evidence.
checklist.done: every FCIC notice has a same-day issue, a computed 45-day deadline, linked record entries and in-window acceptance evidence.

checklist.step: Coordinate with RMA on disputed or unclear edits
actions: Where the team believes a rejected record is actually correct, document the position with the source evidence and the edit-spec reading before contacting RMA.
Raise the question through the RMA help desk or the regional office contact, recording ticket number, date and the RMA answer verbatim.
Apply RMA's answer to all similar records, updating the local edit mirror where RMA's interpretation differs from ours.
Have Regulatory Counsel review before any dispute is escalated formally.
checklist.done: each disputed edit shows a documented position, an RMA ticket and answer, and a mirror update where needed.

checklist.step: Feed systemic causes back into the C18 rule pack
actions: Each month, rank the quarter-to-date edit codes by rejection volume and identify any code the local mirror should have caught pre-submission.
Raise a rule-pack change request for each gap so the failure is caught before submission next cycle.
Verify with the Data Engineer that the previous month's rule additions actually reduced that code's reject count.
Record the feedback loop outcome in the monthly quality note.
checklist.done: mirror gaps become rule-pack changes and the note evidences reject counts falling for previously added rules.

checklist.step: Keep claims-side rejects aligned with section 14 requirements
actions: For loss-record rejects, re-verify the underlying claim against 7 CFR 457.8 section 14 before correcting: company form meeting FCIC standards, complete indemnity-calculation elements and a rostered adjuster id.
Correct the claim record in the Claims Platform and route any adjuster-roster gap to the Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager.
Confirm no indemnity was paid on a claim whose record cannot be made section 14 complete; if one was, escalate to the Claims Director / Manager and Compliance the same day.
Reference the exception-log id on every claim correction.
checklist.done: loss-record corrections are section-14-verified, roster gaps are routed, and any paid-but-incomplete claim was escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Report the reject cycle in the weekly crop-reporting stand-up
actions: Bring to the weekly stand-up: new rejects by edit code, corrections completed, records riding the next cutoff, repeats and aged items.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst that the resubmission set is in the batch before the noon-on-cutoff check.
Flag to the Data Quality Manager anything that will miss the next cutoff, before the cutoff.
Note the stand-up summary on the weekly log.
checklist.done: the stand-up note shows the week's reject flow and pre-cutoff confirmation of the resubmission set.

checklist.step: Reconcile the exception log to PASS reports monthly
actions: Each month, total the rejected records on the month's PASS processing reports and reconcile to exception-log entries created — any report reject without a log entry is a control failure.
Reconcile closures: every 'closed — accepted' entry must reference a receipt covering that record.
Sign the monthly reconciliation and file it.
Raise a tracker issue for any reconciliation break.
checklist.done: the signed monthly reconciliation ties log entries to PASS reports both ways with breaks raised as issues.

checklist.step: Maintain the correction runbook and cross-train the team
actions: Keep the runbook current: edit-spec lookup path, triage categories, correction routing, resubmission mechanics, 45-day clock handling and RMA contact routes.
Cross-train a second analyst on the full cycle and record a supervised live run twice a year.
Update the runbook within 5 business days of any Appendix III edit-spec change.
Have the Data Engineer peer-review pipeline-related sections.
checklist.done: the runbook is current, a trained backup has recorded live runs, and edit-spec changes land within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Archive the reject-cycle evidence
actions: File the quarter's processing reports, exception-log extract, monthly reconciliations, RMA correspondence and 45-day clock evidence under REG-056/C20/<reinsurance year>.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label.
Verify retrievability by edit code, record key and batch id.
Confirm the Records Manager's index includes the folder.
checklist.done: the quarter's evidence is filed, labelled and retrievable by edit code, record key and batch.

testing.step: Build the reject population from PASS reports, not the exception log
actions: Collect every PASS/eDAS processing report for the quarter from the evidence repository and total the rejected/edit-failed records per week.
Separately list all FCIC-directed correction notices received in the quarter from RMA correspondence.
Record the population counts before opening the team's exception log.
testing.done: an independent reject population and FCIC-notice list exist with documented counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the exception log both ways
actions: Match every report reject to a log entry on record key + batch id; report rejects without entries are automatic exceptions.
Check entry creation timestamps against report retrieval timestamps — anything over 1 business day is an intake failure.
Match log entries back to report lines to catch entries with no PASS source.
testing.done: the log reconciles to the reports both ways with intake timeliness computed per entry.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of rejects
actions: Take 100% of repeat rejections, 100% of FCIC-noticed items and 100% of entries aged past 14 days, plus a seeded random 25 standard rejects.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
File the sample list in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all repeats, FCIC items and aged entries plus 25 random rejects is drawn.

testing.step: Re-perform the edit-code triage on sampled rejects
actions: For each sampled reject, look up the edit code in the current-year Appendix III edit specification and reach an independent root-cause category before reading the team's triage.
Compare category, owner routing and severity to the log entry; differences are exceptions.
Capture the edit-spec extract used into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled reject carries an independent triage note compared against the recorded one.

testing.step: Trace sampled corrections to the system of record
actions: Open each sampled record's change history in the Policy Administration Platform or Claims Platform and verify the named field was corrected there, referencing the exception-log id.
Confirm no correction was made by editing the extract or submission file directly.
Verify the corrected value against underlying documents (application, acreage report, claim file) rather than accepting the change at face value.
testing.done: sampled corrections are evidenced in source change histories with values verified to underlying documents.

testing.step: Trace sampled resubmissions to PASS acceptance
actions: For each sampled record, find the resubmission batch and open its PASS acceptance receipt, confirming the record key appears as accepted.
Recompute resubmission timeliness: correction date versus the next weekly transaction cutoff after it.
Verify the log closure date and receipt reference match the receipt itself.
testing.done: sampled records trace to accepted resubmissions with timeliness recomputed and closures matching receipts.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day clocks on all FCIC-noticed items
actions: For every FCIC notice, recompute the deadline as notice date plus 45 days from the notice document itself.
Compare against the PASS acceptance dates of every linked record; any acceptance after day 45 is a reportable breach.
Verify the day-30 CDO and day-40 Head of Compliance escalations fired where items were still open.
testing.done: all FCIC clocks are recomputed with in-window closure evidenced, escalations verified, or breaches reported.

testing.step: Test the repeat-rejection and full-book sweep controls
actions: For each repeat rejection, verify a root-cause analysis by the Data Engineer exists and the fix was released before the record's second resubmission.
For sampled mapping-defect fixes, verify the full-book sweep found and corrected sibling records, not just the rejected ones, by re-running the sweep query.
Check the rule-pack feedback loop: codes added last quarter should show falling reject counts this quarter.
testing.done: repeats show pre-resubmission root-cause fixes, sweeps are re-performed, and the feedback loop shows falling counts.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing record key, edit code, the Appendix III requirement and the impact.
Assign root cause (intake gap, triage error, source-fix bypass, clock breach) with a named owner and remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Score the quarter against the thresholds: 100% 1-day intake, 95% next-cutoff resubmission, zero 45-day breaches, zero unresolved repeats.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — who worked or approved none of the sampled items — sign the workpaper.
Report to the Chief Data Officer and Compliance Committee and file under REG-056/C20.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring the quarter against thresholds is filed and reported.
