checklist.step: Maintain the REG-056 file plan in the repository
actions: Keep the file plan structured as REG-056/<obligation: C17-C24>/<reinsurance year>/<batch id or filing name>, with naming conventions documented for receipts, validation reports and correspondence.
Restrict write access to the named archivists and pipeline service accounts; everything else is read-only.
Enable version history and immutable timestamps on the archive libraries.
Review the file plan each July against any new obligation added to the C17 calendar.
checklist.done: the file plan matches the documented structure, write access is restricted, and versioning is enabled.

checklist.step: Define what a complete submission record contains
actions: Publish the completeness definition per submission type: weekly batch = batch files reference, validation report, hand-off receipt, PASS acceptance receipt, any reject report; Plan of Operations = full Appendix II package, sign-offs, portal confirmation, FCIC acceptance; monthly report = report, reviewer sign-off, confirmation.
Agree the definition with the Regulatory Reporting Manager and Data Quality Manager so intake can be checked mechanically.
Version the definition and note the SRA citation behind each element.
Re-issue on any Appendix II/III change.
checklist.done: a versioned, agreed completeness definition exists per submission type with citations.

checklist.step: Ingest each week's submission set within 5 business days
actions: Each week, collect from the C19 evidence folder the batch's receipt, validation report and any reject report, and file them into the file-plan location for that batch id.
Run the completeness checklist against the submission-type definition and record the check on the intake log.
Chase the Regulatory Reporting Analyst the same day for any missing element.
Timestamp intake completion — the 5-business-day clock runs from the submission date.
checklist.done: the week's set is filed complete within 5 business days with the checklist recorded, or a chase is logged.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label at intake
actions: Stamp every archived item with the retention rule: earliest disposal 3 years after the end of the reinsurance year the record belongs to (June 30 + 3 years).
Verify the reinsurance-year attribute on the item is correct — a wrong year silently shortens retention.
Apply the extended-retention flag where the item relates to an open FCIC review, audit finding or claim dispute.
Record label application in the intake log.
checklist.done: every item carries the correct reinsurance-year retention label with extensions applied where flagged.

checklist.step: Overlay legal and regulator holds immediately when notified
actions: On any hold notice from General Counsel or an RMA review notification from the Regulatory Reporting Manager, apply the hold flag to the affected folders the same business day.
Confirm the hold suppresses disposition in the repository by checking a held item's disposition eligibility.
Acknowledge the hold in writing to the issuer with the scope applied.
Track active holds on the hold register and re-verify them quarterly.
checklist.done: holds are applied same-day, verified to suppress disposition, acknowledged, and registered.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to the submission log monthly
actions: Each month, take the C19 submission log rows for the month and verify each maps to a complete archive folder.
Compute the intake lag per row and list any over 5 business days.
Sign the reconciliation and file it; raise a tracker issue for any missing folder.
Report chronic lag sources to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the signed monthly reconciliation maps every submission to a complete folder with lags computed and gaps raised.

checklist.step: Protect PII inside the archive
actions: Confirm archive folders containing producer SSN/EIN or other Protected Information carry the restricted-access classification and are excluded from broad search scopes.
Review the archive access list quarterly against the approved matrix and remove drift.
Report any unauthorized access or suspected loss immediately to the Privacy Officer for the one-hour FCIC report clock under Appendix III.
Record the quarterly review in the privacy evidence folder.
checklist.done: restricted classification is verified, the quarterly access review is recorded, and the one-hour escalation path is live.

checklist.step: Run the semi-annual retrieval drill
actions: Twice a year, have someone outside the records team request 5 specific items (e.g. 'the PASS receipt for the week ending X', 'the Plan of Operations sign-off for year Y').
Fulfil each request and measure elapsed time against the 5-business-day regulator SLA.
Verify the retrieved items open, are complete and match the request.
Log the drill results and fix any retrieval failure as an exception.
checklist.done: the drill retrieved all 5 items complete and in-SLA, or failures are logged as exceptions.

checklist.step: Verify backup and recoverability of the archive
actions: Confirm the repository's archive libraries are in the backup scope with the retention-aware backup policy applied.
Restore one archived submission folder to an isolated location annually and verify integrity against the live copy.
Report the restore-test result to the Records Manager for the evidence file.
Flag any archive library found outside backup scope the day it is found.
checklist.done: backup scope is confirmed and the annual restore test verified an intact folder.

checklist.step: Control disposition at the end of retention
actions: Each July, generate the disposition-eligible list: folders past 3 years after their reinsurance-year end with no hold or extension flag.
Route the list to Head of Compliance and General Counsel for written approval before any disposal executes.
Execute approved disposals through the repository's audited disposition function, never manual deletion.
File the approved list and the disposition certificates.
checklist.done: disposals happen only from an approved list via the audited function, with certificates filed.

checklist.step: Serve RMA and examiner document requests from the archive
actions: On an RMA or examiner request routed by the Regulatory Reporting Manager, log the request, scope and due date.
Assemble the production set from the archive, have the Regulatory Reporting Manager verify it answers the request, and Regulatory Counsel clear it before release.
Deliver within the requested window, defaulting to 5 business days, and record what was produced and when.
Keep the production set as its own archived record.
checklist.done: each request shows a logged scope, a counsel-cleared production within the window, and an archived production set.

checklist.step: Archive the supporting detail behind the numbers, not just the receipts
actions: For each weekly batch, verify the archive links to the reconciliation worksheet and validation report that support the submitted figures, and to the exception-log extract for any rejects.
For the Plan of Operations, verify the archived package includes the underlying CFO-signed retained-premium and fund-designation workings.
Reject an intake as incomplete where only the receipt is present.
Record the supporting-detail check on the intake log.
checklist.done: every archived submission links to its supporting detail, and receipt-only intakes were rejected.

checklist.step: Track archive exceptions to closure
actions: Log every missing item, late intake, failed retrieval, access drift and hold issue as a tracker item with root cause and owner.
Review open items monthly with Head of Compliance.
Close items only with evidence (the recovered document, the fixed access list, the passed re-retrieval).
Trend exception causes annually into procedure changes.
checklist.done: every archive exception is tracked with root cause and closed on evidence, with causes trended annually.

checklist.step: Train archivists and cover absences
actions: Keep the archiving runbook current: file plan, completeness definitions, labelling rules, hold handling and retrieval SLA.
Train a backup archivist and record a supervised intake cycle twice a year.
Update the runbook within 5 business days of any file-plan or retention-schedule change.
Have the Document Management Specialist peer-review updates.
checklist.done: the runbook is current and a trained backup has recorded supervised cycles.

checklist.step: Report archive health annually
actions: Compile the annual archive-health report: intake timeliness, completeness rate, retrieval drill results, restore test, holds, disposals and exceptions.
Present it to Head of Compliance after each reinsurance-year close.
Minute agreed actions with owners and dates.
File the report in the evidence repository under REG-056/C21.
checklist.done: the annual report is presented, actions are minuted with owners, and the report is filed.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions that should be archived
actions: Take the reinsurance year's C19 submission log as the population: every weekly batch, monthly report and the Plan of Operations.
Cross-check the log against PASS acceptance receipts held in the compliance evidence repository so the population does not depend on the archive being tested.
Record the population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: a submission population independent of the archive is built and counted.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to archive folders
actions: Verify each population row maps to an archive folder in the correct file-plan location.
Compute the intake lag for each from submission date to intake timestamp; lags over 5 business days are exceptions.
List any folder with no population source for validity checking.
testing.done: every submission maps to a correctly located folder with intake lag computed, or is an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of archived records
actions: Select the Plan of Operations (100%), a seeded random 10 weekly batches and 3 monthly reports, plus every folder that had an exception during the year.
Record seed, population and selection date.
File the sample list.
testing.done: a reproducible sample including the Plan and all prior-exception folders is drawn.

testing.step: Test completeness of each sampled folder against the definition
actions: Open each sampled folder and check every element the completeness definition demands: receipts, validation reports, sign-offs, correspondence and supporting workings.
Open each document to confirm it is readable and is the document its name claims.
A folder holding only a receipt fails, per the supporting-detail rule.
testing.done: each sampled folder demonstrates full, readable content against the definition, or fails.

testing.step: Verify retention labels and reinsurance-year attribution
actions: For each sampled item, recompute the correct earliest-disposal date (reinsurance-year end June 30 + 3 years) and compare to the applied label.
Verify the reinsurance-year attribute matches the submission's actual year from the receipt.
Check extended-retention flags exist where the item relates to a known open FCIC review or dispute.
testing.done: labels and year attribution recompute correctly on every sampled item.

testing.step: Perform an unannounced retrieval test
actions: Request 5 specific items from the Records Manager without notice, phrased as an examiner would ('the acceptance receipt for the week ending X').
Measure elapsed time to complete delivery against the 5-business-day SLA.
Verify delivered items match the requests exactly.
testing.done: all 5 unannounced retrievals delivered matching items within the SLA, or failures are logged.

testing.step: Test hold handling and the disposition trail
actions: For each active hold on the register, verify the hold flag is on the folders and disposition eligibility is suppressed.
Inspect the year's disposition run: approved list, Head of Compliance and General Counsel approvals pre-dating execution, and disposition certificates from the audited function.
Attempt to locate any item disposed outside the approved list — any hit is a reportable breach.
testing.done: holds verifiably suppress disposition and every disposal traces to pre-approved, certificated execution.

testing.step: Verify access restrictions and the restore test
actions: Pull the archive access list and compare to the approved matrix; drift is an exception.
Verify the quarterly privacy access reviews and the annual restore test were performed and recorded, re-checking the restore evidence.
Confirm PII folders carry the restricted classification by inspecting three of them.
testing.done: access matches the matrix, reviews and restore tests are evidenced, and PII classification is confirmed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing the folder, the retention requirement and the impact.
Assign root cause (intake gap, labelling error, retrieval failure, access drift, disposition control) with a named owner and date.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Score against the thresholds: 100% archived complete in 5 business days, 100% retrieval success, zero improper disposals.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — who administers no part of the repository — sign the workpaper.
Report to Head of Compliance and the Compliance Committee and file under REG-056/C21.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring the archive against thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the trigger-point map for privacy notices in the crop line
actions: Keep a documented map of every point where Protected Information or PII is collected from a producer: application/enrollment, acreage report, production report, claim intake, adverse decision letters and the producer portal registration.

For each trigger point, record which statement is required (Privacy Act statement, USDA nondiscrimination statement, or both), the delivery channel (printed form, portal screen, letter) and the responsible operational team.
Review the map with the Insurance Product Manager and Claims Director / Manager annually and on any new producer-facing process.
Publish the current map to the operational teams on the crop SharePoint site.
checklist.done: a published trigger-point map names the statement, channel and owning team for every collection point.

checklist.step: Verify the approved statement wording at every RMA edition release
actions: On each RMA form-edition release or Manual 14 update flagged by the C17 bulletin sweep, pull the new specimen and read the Privacy Act statement (5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(3) elements: authority, purpose, routine uses, effect of not providing) and the USDA nondiscrimination statement word for word.
Diff the wording against the statements currently printing from the Policy Administration Platform.
Where wording changed, open a form-change request the same day with the RMA mandatory-use date attached.
File the diff and the specimen in the notice evidence folder.
checklist.done: every edition release shows a wording diff on file and, where changed, a same-day form-change request with the mandatory-use date.

checklist.step: Deploy statement changes to the form templates before the mandatory-use date
actions: Update the application, acreage report, claim and letter templates in the Policy Administration Platform's form library with the new statement text, keeping the RMA-required placement and prominence.
Generate a test document from each updated template and proof the statement text character-for-character against the RMA specimen.
Schedule the release so production documents carry the new edition on or before the RMA mandatory-use date, and retire the old edition the same day.
Record the deployment date and release id against the form-change request.
checklist.done: updated templates are proofed against the specimen and live on or before the mandatory-use date with the old edition retired.

checklist.step: Push refreshed materials to agents and the portal in the same cycle
actions: Replace downloadable applications, claim forms and enrollment packets on the Broker & Agent Portal with the new edition and remove the superseded files no later than the transaction cutoff week in which the edition changes.
Send the agency channel a notice naming the new edition, the mandatory-use date and the instruction to destroy stale stock.
Track acknowledgment from each agency principal in the distribution log.
Spot-download three documents from the portal after the swap to confirm the live files are the new edition.
checklist.done: portal files are swapped, the agency notice is acknowledged in the log, and spot-downloads confirm the new edition.

checklist.step: Keep the producer portal and website notices current
actions: Verify the producer self-service portal shows the privacy notice and nondiscrimination statement at registration and before any PII entry screen.
Check the crop-line pages of the public website link to the current notice version.
Re-verify both after every portal release, using the release notes from the Digital Channel Manager as the trigger.
Screenshot the live screens into the notice evidence folder with dates.
checklist.done: portal and website notices are verified current after each release with dated screenshots on file.

checklist.step: Confirm notice presence at application intake
actions: At policy issuance, verify the signed application image in the document repository is the current edition and shows the Privacy Act and nondiscrimination statements.
Reject applications submitted on superseded editions past the mandatory-use date back to the agent for re-execution on the current form.
Log each rejection with agency, form edition received and resolution.
Flag repeat-offending agencies to the Agency Relations Manager monthly.
checklist.done: issued policies carry current-edition signed applications and stale-edition submissions are rejected and logged.

checklist.step: Confirm notice delivery at claim intake
actions: At first notice of loss, use the current claim-intake script and form carrying the required statements, whether intake is by phone, portal or paper.
For phone intake, read the scripted notice reference and record the delivery flag on the claim record.
For paper and portal intake, verify the form edition on the received document before accepting it into the claim file.
Route any intake received without the notice to the Claims Coordinator for corrective delivery to the producer.
checklist.done: every new claim record carries a notice-delivery flag or a corrective-delivery entry.

checklist.step: Log notice deliveries into the notice record
actions: Maintain the notice log: per trigger event, the policy or claim number, trigger type, form edition or script version used, delivery date and channel.
Feed the log automatically from the Policy Administration and Claims platforms' document-generation events where possible; enter manual channels weekly.
Reconcile log volume monthly against issued-policy and opened-claim counts to catch silent gaps.
File the monthly reconciliation.
checklist.done: the notice log covers all trigger events with a monthly volume reconciliation on file.

checklist.step: Instruct and attest the agency channel annually
actions: Include notice-delivery duties in the annual agency compliance communication: use current editions only, deliver the statements at collection, never strip pages from applications.
Collect an annual attestation from each agency principal covering notice delivery.
Chase non-attesting agencies at 30 days and suspend new-business submission rights for refusal, per the agency agreement.
File attestations in the distribution log.
checklist.done: annual agency attestations are collected, chased at 30 days, and filed.

checklist.step: Handle notice-related complaints and questions
actions: Tag any producer complaint alleging missing or misleading privacy/nondiscrimination notices with the privacy-notice category.
Route tagged complaints to the Privacy Officer within 2 business days for investigation against the notice log.
Where the notice genuinely failed, deliver the corrective notice and record it, and feed the failure into the exception log.
Report tagged complaint counts to the DPO quarterly.
checklist.done: notice complaints are tagged, routed within 2 business days, remediated where founded, and reported quarterly.

checklist.step: Control template drift with quarterly specimen checks
actions: Quarterly, generate a live specimen of each producer-facing template and compare its statement text character-for-character against the controlled RMA specimen.
Verify the form-edition identifier printing in the footer matches the current approved edition.
Log the check per template and open a form-change request for any drift found.
File the quarterly specimen set as evidence.
checklist.done: quarterly specimens match the controlled wording and edition identifiers, with drift raised same-day.

checklist.step: Train intake and claims staff on notice obligations
actions: Run annual training for policy issuance, claims intake and contact-center staff covering the trigger-point map, current statements and rejection/corrective procedures.
Track completion in the learning management system and chase to 100% within the training window.
Refresh the module within 30 days of any statement-wording change.
Report completion rates to the Privacy Officer.
checklist.done: annual training reaches 100% completion and the module reflects current wording within 30 days of change.

checklist.step: Log and remediate every notice failure
actions: Record every identified failure (missing statement, stale edition past mandatory date, unflagged intake) with policy/claim reference, trigger point and root cause.
Deliver the corrective notice to the affected producer and record the corrective delivery date.
Assess clusters with Privacy Counsel for any reporting or systemic-remediation obligation.
Obtain DPO sign-off on each closure.
checklist.done: every failure shows corrective delivery, root cause, counsel assessment where clustered, and DPO-signed closure.

checklist.step: Coordinate with the one-hour incident path when notices intersect a breach
actions: Where a notice failure coincides with a loss or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Information or PII, invoke the Appendix III incident path: report to FCIC within one hour of discovery, suspected or confirmed alike.
Keep the FCIC incident-report contact route and template on the incident quick-card referenced by the notice procedure.
Rehearse the one-hour path once a year with the Incident Response Lead and record the drill.
File any actual report and its timeline evidence.
checklist.done: the one-hour path is documented on the quick-card, drilled annually, and any actual report is filed with its timeline.

checklist.step: Archive notice evidence for the retention period
actions: File specimens, deployment confirmations, distribution logs, attestations, training records and the notice log monthly under REG-056/C22/<reinsurance year>.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label.
Verify retrievability by policy number, form edition and trigger type.
Hand the index to the Records Manager for the C21 archive.
checklist.done: notice evidence is filed monthly, retention-labelled, and retrievable by policy, edition and trigger.

testing.step: Build the trigger-event population for the period
actions: Extract from the Policy Administration Platform all applications signed and policies issued in the period, and from the Claims Platform all claims opened, by month and channel.
Add adverse-decision letters issued, from the correspondence log.
Reconcile the counts to the notice log's monthly reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: a reconciled population of applications, claims and adverse decisions exists by month and channel.

testing.step: Reconcile the notice log against the population
actions: Match population events to notice-log entries; any trigger event without a log entry or corrective-delivery record is an exception.
Check manual-channel entries were logged within the weekly window.
List and count gaps by trigger type and channel.
testing.done: every trigger event matches a notice-log or corrective entry, with gaps counted by type.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across trigger points and channels
actions: Select a seeded random sample: 25 applications, 15 claims and 5 adverse-decision letters, stratified across paper, portal and phone channels and across agencies.
Include 100% of events in the month following any form-edition change.
Record seed, strata and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample including the post-edition-change month is drawn.

testing.step: Inspect the actual documents for verbatim statements
actions: Open the signed application, claim form or letter image for each sampled event in the document repository.
Compare the Privacy Act statement and USDA nondiscrimination statement on the document character-for-character against the RMA specimen in force on the document date.
Verify the form-edition identifier in the footer was the approved edition for that date — a current statement on a stale edition still fails.
Capture each compared page into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled document shows verbatim statements on the in-force edition, with pages captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the phone-intake notice check
actions: For sampled phone-intake claims, pull the call recording from the contact-center platform and listen for the scripted notice delivery.
Compare the delivery flag on the claim record to what the recording shows.
A flag set with no notice audible on the recording is a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: sampled recordings evidence the scripted notice matching the claim-record flags.

testing.step: Verify edition-deployment timeliness against RMA mandatory-use dates
actions: For each form-edition change in the period, compare the template deployment date and portal file-swap date against the RMA mandatory-use date from the bulletin.
Search the document repository for any document generated on the old edition after the mandatory-use date.
Verify the agency notice and stale-stock instruction went out in the cutoff week of the change.
testing.done: deployments pre-date mandatory-use dates and no post-date old-edition documents exist, or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Test portal and website notice presence as a producer would see it
actions: Walk the producer portal registration and claim-submission flows and confirm the notice appears before any PII entry screen.
Verify the public crop pages link to the current notice version.
Screenshot each verified screen into the workpaper with dates.
testing.done: live flows show the notice pre-PII-entry with dated screenshots captured.

testing.step: Verify training, attestations and complaint handling
actions: Pull LMS completion for the annual notice training and verify 100% for in-scope staff, including joiners within their window.
Sample 5 agency attestations and verify chase actions for late agencies.
Trace all privacy-notice-tagged complaints in the period to investigations and, where founded, corrective deliveries.
testing.done: training completion, attestation coverage and complaint traces are evidenced, or gaps listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing the policy/claim, trigger point, the Manual 14/Appendix IV or Privacy Act element missed, and the impact.
Assign root cause (template drift, stale stock, script skip, log gap) with a named owner and remediation date.
Require corrective notice delivery for every affected producer and carry open items into the next test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, corrective delivery and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Score against the thresholds: 100% verbatim statements on in-force editions, zero post-mandatory-date usage.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — outside the Privacy Office and form deployment — sign the workpaper.
Report to the DPO and Compliance Committee and file under REG-056/C22.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Operate defined intake channels and standardize receipt
actions: Monitor the published intake channels daily: the privacy web form, the privacy mailbox, the contact-center privacy queue and postal mail routed by the Correspondence Clerk.

Open a case for every request the day it arrives, recording receipt date, channel, requester identity claim, request type (access, correction, restriction, deletion) and the crop policies or claims referenced.
Instruct agents via the Broker & Agent Portal notice that producer requests they receive must be relayed to the privacy mailbox within 2 business days, and log the relay date as the receipt date.
Start the 45-day SLA timer from the receipt date on every case.
checklist.done: every request from every channel has a same-day case with receipt date, type, scope and a running SLA timer.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the requester within 3 business days
actions: Send the templated acknowledgment stating what was requested, the identity evidence needed, and the 45-day response window.
Use the requester's verified channel of contact; never send acknowledgment content that itself reveals PII.
Record the acknowledgment timestamp on the case.
Chase any case unacknowledged at day 2 via the daily queue review.
checklist.done: every case shows an acknowledgment timestamp within 3 business days of receipt.

checklist.step: Verify identity proportionally to the data at stake
actions: Apply the verification matrix: policyholder portal login plus a policy-detail challenge for standard access; notarized or documentary proof for SSN-bearing or full-file requests; written authorization plus verification for authorized representatives (e.g. estate executors, attorneys-in-fact).
Match the requester against the policy record in the Policy Administration Platform — name, address history and policy number must corroborate.
Record the evidence type reviewed (never store copies of full government IDs longer than the verification requires) and the pass/fail outcome.
Refuse fulfilment and record the rationale where verification fails, offering the requester another attempt.
checklist.done: every fulfilled case carries a passed, evidenced verification matched to the policy record; failures are recorded with rationale.

checklist.step: Determine company records versus FCIC systems of records
actions: For each verified request, determine which requested records the company holds in its own right (application files, claim files, correspondence) and which live in FCIC/RMA systems of records under the Privacy Act.
For FCIC-held records, give the requester the USDA/RMA Privacy Act request route in writing rather than attempting to answer for the government, and record the referral.
For company-held copies of data already reported to RMA, fulfil from the company's records and note that RMA holds its own copy.
Log the determination and its basis on the case.
checklist.done: each case shows a documented company-versus-FCIC determination with referrals recorded where FCIC owns the records.

checklist.step: Locate the requester's data across the crop systems
actions: Search the Policy Administration Platform by policy number and tax id for policy, acreage and production records; search the Claims Platform for claim files; query the enterprise data warehouse via the data inventory for derived copies.
Use the C24 processing register as the checklist of stores to search so no repository is missed.
Compile the hit list with system, record type and date range per hit.
Have the Data Steward confirm the warehouse search covered all crop-domain schemas.
checklist.done: a register-driven hit list covers every in-scope store with the warehouse search confirmed by the Data Steward.

checklist.step: Assemble and redact the access package
actions: Compile the responsive records into the fulfilment package, redacting third parties' PII (other producers on shared units, adjuster personal contact details) and any FCIC-restricted material.
Have the Privacy Officer second-review every package before release — no single-person releases.
Record what was included, what was withheld and the withholding basis on the case.
Release through a secure channel (portal download or encrypted delivery), never plain email attachments.
checklist.done: each released package is second-reviewed, redaction-logged, and delivered through a secure channel.

checklist.step: Process correction requests against the source systems
actions: Validate the claimed error against source documents (application, acreage report, claim file) before changing anything.
Apply approved corrections in the Policy Administration Platform or Claims Platform with the DSAR case id referenced on the change.
Where the correction is refused (the record is accurate), draft the refusal with the evidence and have Privacy Counsel review before sending.
Notify the requester of the outcome within the 45-day window either way.
checklist.done: corrections are evidence-validated, applied at source with case id, or refused with counsel-reviewed rationale — all within SLA.

checklist.step: Propagate corrections to RMA through the weekly cycle
actions: For any corrected field that was previously reported to RMA, queue the corrected record into the next weekly PASS batch under the C18/C19 cycle, no later than the next transaction cutoff after the correction is approved.
Track the resubmission to its PASS acceptance receipt and record the receipt reference on the DSAR case.
Confirm to the requester that the correction has been transmitted to the federal record where they asked about it.
Flag any correction not accepted by PASS back to the C20 exception process.
checklist.done: every RMA-relevant correction rode the next cutoff with the acceptance receipt referenced on the case.

checklist.step: Manage the 45-day clock and permitted extensions
actions: Work the SLA dashboard daily; the timers alert at day 10, 30 (Privacy Officer escalation) and 40 (DPO escalation).
Where the applicable statute permits an extension and the case genuinely needs one, document the reason, extend once by no more than 45 days, and notify the requester before day 45 with the new date.
Never extend for internal convenience — capacity problems escalate to the Privacy Officer for reallocation instead.
Record closure date and elapsed days on every case.
checklist.done: no case passes day 45 without a documented, notified, permitted extension, and closures carry elapsed-day counts.

checklist.step: Handle restriction and deletion requests within federal constraints
actions: For deletion/restriction requests, check the retention constraints first: records required under the SRA and Appendix III (3 years after the reinsurance year) and litigation holds cannot be deleted, and the refusal must say so with the citation.
Where deletion is permissible (e.g. marketing copies, expired non-required data), execute it via the Data Steward and record the scope.
Apply processing restrictions (suppression flags) where the data must be kept but not used beyond the federal purpose.
Have Privacy Counsel review every refusal before it is sent.
checklist.done: deletion outcomes respect SRA retention with cited refusals counsel-reviewed, and permissible deletions/restrictions are executed and recorded.

checklist.step: Maintain the DSAR log as the single record of requests
actions: Keep one log row per request: receipt date, channel, type, verification outcome, determination, fulfilment/refusal, key dates and elapsed days.
Reconcile the log monthly against channel sources (web form submissions, privacy mailbox, contact-center queue) to catch unlogged requests.
Sign the monthly reconciliation and file it.
Report volumes, SLA performance and refusal reasons to the DPO quarterly.
checklist.done: the log reconciles to all channels monthly and the quarterly DPO report is issued.

checklist.step: Train front-line staff to recognize and route requests
actions: Train contact-center, claims and policy-service staff annually to recognize a rights request in any wording and route it to the privacy queue the same day.
Include the rule that nobody outside the DSAR desk releases PII in response to a request, however simple it looks.
Track completion to 100% in the learning management system.
Refresh the module on any procedure change.
checklist.done: annual recognition training reaches 100% and routing lands requests in the queue same-day.

checklist.step: Escalate wrongful-disclosure near misses to the incident path
actions: Treat any disclosure without completed verification, or to the wrong recipient, as a potential loss of PII: invoke the Appendix III one-hour FCIC report path immediately upon discovery, suspected or confirmed.
Contain the disclosure (recall, secure-delete confirmation from recipient) and record the timeline.
Run the root-cause review with the DPO and feed fixes into the verification matrix.
File the incident record with the timeline evidence.
checklist.done: any wrongful disclosure shows a one-hour FCIC report, containment, root cause and a filed timeline.

checklist.step: Review the procedure annually against changing law
actions: Annually re-verify the SLA and rights matrix against the current Privacy Act guidance, USDA/RMA requirements and the state privacy statutes applicable to the producer footprint.
Update the procedure, templates and refusal citations where the law moved.
Brief the DSAR desk on changes within 30 days of the review.
Record the review date and outcome in the procedure history.
checklist.done: the annual legal review is recorded with procedure updates briefed to the desk within 30 days.

checklist.step: Archive DSAR evidence for the retention period
actions: File closed-case packages, the DSAR log extract, monthly reconciliations and quarterly reports under REG-056/C23/<reinsurance year>.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label, keeping identity documents only as long as verification requires.
Verify retrievability by requester, policy number and case id.
Hand the index to the Records Manager for the C21 archive.
checklist.done: DSAR evidence is filed, minimally retentive on identity documents, and retrievable by requester and case.

testing.step: Build the request population from channel sources, not the log
actions: Pull the period's privacy web-form submissions, privacy-mailbox items, contact-center privacy-queue records and logged postal routings directly from each channel system.
De-duplicate into a request population with receipt dates per channel.
Record the population count before opening the DSAR log.
testing.done: an independent, de-duplicated request population with receipt dates exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the DSAR log
actions: Match every population item to a case; channel items with no case are automatic exceptions.
Verify receipt dates on cases match the channel timestamps — a late-entered receipt date shortens the apparent SLA and is an exception.
Check agent-relayed requests used the relay receipt date, not the desk-arrival date.
testing.done: every channel item matches a case with a truthful receipt date, or is an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of requests
actions: Take 100% of refusals, extensions, deletion requests and any case closed after day 40, plus a seeded random 20 access and 10 correction cases.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
File the sample list.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all refusals, extensions and late closures plus a random spread is drawn.

testing.step: Recompute the SLA clocks on every sampled case
actions: Recompute acknowledgment elapsed days (receipt to acknowledgment; threshold 3 business days) and fulfilment elapsed days (receipt to closure; threshold 45 calendar days) from raw timestamps.
For extended cases, verify the extension was permitted, documented and notified to the requester before day 45.
Any closure past 45 days without a compliant extension is a fail.
testing.done: all sampled clocks are recomputed from raw timestamps with extensions verified compliant.

testing.step: Re-perform identity verification review on sampled fulfilments
actions: For each sampled fulfilled case, inspect the recorded verification evidence type and outcome against the verification matrix for the data sensitivity involved.
Confirm the requester was corroborated against the policy record and, for representatives, that written authorization was on file before release.
Any release preceding completed verification is a wrongful-disclosure finding, escalated immediately.
testing.done: every sampled release shows matrix-compliant, pre-release verification, or a wrongful-disclosure finding is raised.

testing.step: Test completeness of data location against the processing register
actions: For 5 sampled access cases, re-run the search across every store the C24 processing register lists for producer PII.
Compare hits to the case's hit list; responsive records the desk missed are exceptions.
Verify redactions in the released package against the withholding log.
testing.done: re-run searches match the case hit lists and redactions match the withholding log.

testing.step: Trace sampled corrections to source systems and RMA propagation
actions: Open the change history for each sampled correction and verify the change was applied at source with the case id referenced.
For RMA-reported fields, trace the corrected record into a weekly PASS batch and to its acceptance receipt, checking it made the next cutoff after approval.
Verify refusal cases carry counsel-reviewed rationales with citations.
testing.done: sampled corrections trace to source changes and timely PASS acceptance; refusals carry reviewed rationales.

testing.step: Verify deletion refusals respected federal retention
actions: For each deletion request, check the outcome against the SRA/Appendix III retention constraint: required records refused with citation, permissible deletions actually executed.
For executed deletions, verify the data is gone from the named stores via the Data Steward's deletion evidence.
For restrictions, verify suppression flags are present and effective on a sample query.
testing.done: deletion outcomes align with retention law, executed deletions are evidenced, and restrictions verifiably suppress.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing the case id, the SLA or verification requirement breached, and the impact.
Assign root cause (channel gap, verification shortcut, search miss, propagation miss) with a named owner and remediation date.
Escalate any wrongful disclosure to the DPO and the incident path the same day.
Carry open exceptions into the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, with disclosures escalated same-day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Score against the thresholds: 100% 3-day acknowledgment, 100% 45-day closure or compliant extension, zero unverified disclosures, zero unpropagated corrections.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — who worked no sampled case — sign the workpaper.
Report to the DPO and Compliance Committee and file under REG-056/C23.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring the desk against thresholds is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Define the register schema and lawful-basis catalogue
actions: Maintain the register schema: activity name, business owner, purpose, data subjects, data elements (flagging SSN/EIN and FCIC Protected Information), systems, recipients (including RMA/FCIC and service providers), retention, security categorization and lawful basis.

Maintain the lawful-basis catalogue with Privacy Counsel: the SRA and 7 CFR part 400/457 authorities for federal reporting, contract performance for policy servicing, and consent where nothing stronger applies — each with its citation text.
Version both artifacts and record counsel's review date.
Publish the schema guidance to activity owners.
checklist.done: a versioned schema and counsel-reviewed lawful-basis catalogue are published to owners.

checklist.step: Enumerate processing activities across the crop value chain
actions: Walk each function with its manager — underwriting, policy servicing, claims and loss adjustment, federal reporting (C18/C19), billing, agency management, training administration — and list every activity touching producer PII or Protected Information.

Include the Appendix IV loss-adjuster training-record administration explicitly: qualification records (60 structured hours including 24 classroom, competency test results) are records subject to FCIC review.
Create or update one register entry per activity from the walk results.
Diarize the walk annually per function.
checklist.done: every function's activities, including adjuster training-record administration, have register entries from a dated walk.

checklist.step: Map data elements and systems for each entry
actions: For each entry, list the data elements processed and link the named systems from the data catalog: Policy Administration Platform, Claims Platform, enterprise data warehouse schemas, HR training stores and any SaaS tools.
Cross-check the system list against the CMDB's application inventory tagged 'crop' so no store is missed.
Flag entries whose elements include SSN/EIN or Protected Information for the restricted-handling overlay.
Have the Data Steward confirm warehouse schema mappings.
checklist.done: each entry lists elements and catalog-linked systems, cross-checked against the CMDB, with sensitive flags applied.

checklist.step: Assign and cite the lawful basis on every entry
actions: Assign each activity a basis from the catalogue and paste the citation onto the entry — e.g. federal reporting activities cite the 2026 SRA Section IV and Appendix III submission duties; claims processing cites the Common Crop Insurance Policy contract and 7 CFR 457.8.
Reject 'legitimate interest'-style generic labels for activities the SRA actually mandates — the stronger, specific basis goes on the entry.
Route unclear cases to Privacy Counsel and record the advice on the entry.
Re-verify citations at each SRA amendment.
checklist.done: every entry carries a specific cited basis, with counsel advice recorded on unclear cases.

checklist.step: Record recipients and cross-border/service-provider flows
actions: On each entry, list every recipient: RMA/FCIC (via PASS submissions), reinsurers, service providers named in the Plan of Operations, adjuster contractors and IT processors.
Verify each service provider appears in the Appendix II service-provider disclosure kept by the Regulatory Reporting Manager, and flag mismatches both ways.
Record the contract or agreement that binds each recipient to confidentiality and FCIC data-handling terms, with the Contracts Manager confirming the clause reference.
Flag any recipient outside the United States for counsel review, given the federal data involved.
checklist.done: recipients are listed with binding-agreement references, reconciled against the Plan of Operations disclosure, and offshore flags reviewed.

checklist.step: Apply FISMA-aligned security categorization to each entry
actions: Categorize each entry's systems for confidentiality/integrity/availability impact consistent with the company's FISMA-aligned obligations under 2026 SRA Section IV(a)(4).
Verify each SSN/EIN-flagged system has current control attestations (access reviews, encryption at rest and in transit) in the GRC platform.
Link the categorization record to the register entry.
Escalate any PII system lacking current attestations to the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: every entry links to a security categorization and PII systems show current control attestations, or escalations are raised.

checklist.step: Gate new systems and process changes on register entry
actions: Enforce the change-process gate: any change ticket introducing a new system or new use of producer PII requires a register entry (or entry update) before go-live approval.
Configure the ITSM workflow so the privacy-review task blocks closure until the Data Privacy Steward links the entry.
Review a monthly report of changes that bypassed the gate and treat each as an exception.
Brief change managers annually on the gate.
checklist.done: the ITSM gate blocks go-live without a linked entry and monthly bypass reports run clean or raise exceptions.

checklist.step: Maintain the adjuster training-record set as FCIC-reviewable records
actions: Record for every new loss adjuster: the structured training hours (at least 60, of which at least 24 classroom) specific to FCIC-approved policy and procedure, and the basic competency test result, before the adjuster is released to adjust claims.
Keep completion certificates and test results in the learning management system linked to the adjuster identifier used on loss records.
Publish the current qualified-adjuster roster to the Claims Director / Manager and the C18 validation team weekly.
Register this record set in the processing register with its FCIC-review lawful basis.
checklist.done: every adjusting-active adjuster shows pre-release 60/24 hours and a passed test in the LMS, with the roster feeding claims validation.

checklist.step: Run the annual owner attestation before July 1
actions: Launch the attestation campaign at T-45 before July 1: each business owner confirms their entries are accurate, complete and still necessary, or submits corrections.
Chase at T-21 and T-7; escalate non-responders to the DPO at T-7.
Apply submitted corrections to the register within 10 business days and version the changes.
Close the campaign with a completion report to the DPO.
checklist.done: 100% of entries carry a current-year owner attestation before July 1, with corrections applied and versioned.

checklist.step: Keep the one-hour incident chain aligned with the register
actions: Verify quarterly that every register entry's systems map to the incident-response scope, so a loss or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Information or PII anywhere registered triggers the Appendix III report to FCIC within one hour of discovery, suspected or confirmed alike.
Confirm the FCIC report route, template and out-of-hours contacts on the incident quick-card match the current RMA instructions.
Run one tabletop a year with the Incident Response Lead using a register-listed system as the scenario.
Record the quarterly check and the drill.
checklist.done: quarterly alignment checks and an annual drill evidence a register-complete one-hour report path.

checklist.step: Sweep for unregistered processing
actions: Semi-annually, scan the data catalog and warehouse schemas for tables holding producer identifiers that no register entry references, using the classification tags.
Review new SaaS purchases with the Procurement Specialist for PII-touching tools that skipped the gate.
Open an exception for every hit and either register the activity or shut the flow down.
Report sweep results to the DPO.
checklist.done: the semi-annual sweep is run with every hit registered or terminated and results reported.

checklist.step: Version the register and minute the governance review
actions: Snapshot the register quarterly with a change log of entries added, amended and retired.
Review the snapshot in the quarterly privacy governance meeting with the DPO, covering attestation status, sweep findings and open exceptions.
Minute decisions with owners and dates.
File snapshots and minutes in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: quarterly snapshots with change logs and minuted governance reviews are on file.

checklist.step: Answer regulator and audit requests from the register
actions: On an RMA, FISMA-review or audit request about data handling, produce the relevant register extract with lawful-basis citations and flows within 5 business days via the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Include the adjuster training-record index where the request touches Appendix IV qualifications.
Have Privacy Counsel clear extracts that reveal gaps before release.
Log each production as its own record.
checklist.done: register-based productions go out within 5 business days, counsel-cleared, and are logged.

checklist.step: Train activity owners on register duties
actions: Deliver annual training to registered business owners on their duties: keep entries current, route changes through the gate, attest annually, and report suspected incidents immediately for the one-hour clock.
Track completion to 100% for owners of SSN/EIN-flagged entries.
Refresh the module on any procedure or SRA change.
Report completion to the DPO with the attestation campaign results.
checklist.done: owner training reaches 100% for sensitive-entry owners and completion is reported with attestations.

checklist.step: Archive register evidence for the retention period
actions: File quarterly snapshots, attestation reports, sweep results, governance minutes and lawful-basis worksheets under REG-056/C24/<reinsurance year>.
Apply the 3-years-after-reinsurance-year retention label; adjuster training records follow the Appendix IV FCIC-review retention instead.
Verify retrievability by activity name, system and owner.
Hand the index to the Records Manager for the C21 archive.
checklist.done: register evidence is filed with the correct dual retention rules and retrievable by activity, system and owner.

testing.step: Build the system population independently of the register
actions: Extract from the CMDB every application tagged to the crop line or integrated with the Policy Administration or Claims platforms.
Extract from the data catalog every schema whose classification tags show producer identifiers or Protected Information.
Merge into a PII-system population with counts recorded before opening the register.
testing.done: an independent PII-system population from CMDB and catalog exists with counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the system population to register entries
actions: Map every population system to at least one register entry; systems with none are unregistered-processing exceptions.
Map register entries back to real systems — entries referencing retired systems are staleness exceptions.
Quantify coverage both ways in the workpaper.
testing.done: two-way system-to-register coverage is quantified with gaps listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of register entries
actions: Take 100% of SSN/EIN-flagged entries plus a seeded random 15 of the remainder, and 100% of entries added since the last test.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
File the sample list.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all sensitive and new entries is drawn.

testing.step: Re-verify the lawful basis and citation on sampled entries
actions: For each sampled entry, read the cited authority (SRA section, 7 CFR provision, contract clause) and independently judge whether it actually covers the described processing.
Flag generic or wrong-strength bases where a specific SRA mandate exists.
Verify counsel advice is recorded on any entry the catalogue marks as judgement-dependent.
testing.done: every sampled basis independently holds up against its citation, or is flagged.

testing.step: Trace sampled entries to reality in the systems
actions: For 5 sampled entries, inspect the named systems and confirm the described data elements and flows actually exist as registered (and nothing materially beyond them).
Verify recipient lists against actual interfaces and the Appendix II service-provider disclosure.
Confirm binding-agreement references resolve to real contract clauses via the Contracts Manager.
testing.done: sampled entries match observed data, flows, recipients and contract clauses.

testing.step: Test the change-gate with tracer changes
actions: Pull the period's change tickets introducing new systems or data uses and verify each shows the privacy-review task completed with a linked register entry before go-live.
Verify the monthly bypass reports ran and that reported bypasses became exceptions.
Any go-live without an entry is an unregistered-processing finding.
testing.done: sampled changes evidence the gate held, bypass reporting ran, and violations are findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the adjuster training-record trace
actions: Select 10 adjusters who adjusted claims in the period from loss-record adjuster identifiers.

For each, verify in the LMS: at least 60 structured training hours including at least 24 classroom hours specific to FCIC-approved policy and procedure, and a passed competency test, all dated before their first adjusted claim.
Verify the weekly qualified-roster feed reached the C18 validation team on the sampled weeks.
Any adjuster active before qualification is a reportable finding.
testing.done: sampled adjusters show pre-activity 60/24-hour records and passed tests, with the roster feed evidenced.

testing.step: Verify attestations, sweeps and the one-hour chain checks
actions: Verify 100% attestation completion before July 1 with escalations evidenced for late owners.
Re-run one semi-annual sweep query and compare hits to the reported results.
Verify the quarterly incident-chain checks and the annual tabletop occurred, inspecting the drill record for the one-hour FCIC report timing.
testing.done: attestation completeness, sweep fidelity and incident-chain drills are independently evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception citing the entry or system, the SRA/FISMA/Appendix IV requirement, and the impact.
Assign root cause (walk gap, gate bypass, stale citation, roster gap) with a named owner and remediation date.
Escalate unregistered sensitive processing and unqualified-adjuster findings to the DPO and Head of Compliance same-day.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date, with sensitive findings escalated same-day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Score against the thresholds: full two-way system coverage, 100% cited bases and attestations, zero unregistered processing, zero unqualified adjusters on claims.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and have the independent reviewer — who maintains no part of the register — sign the workpaper.
Report to the DPO and Compliance Committee and file under REG-056/C24.
testing.done: a signed workpaper scoring the register against thresholds is filed and reported.
